title: Idea Girl and the former band singer Laura Dean
summary: The leading lady of Idea Girl had sung with Barnet at the Glen Island Casino as Laura Dean and ignored him on set.

blocks.x: Let's see, the next picture that is listed here is "Idea Girl," 1946, directed by Will Jason. Light, unpretentious Universal comedy with music, about a music publisher's relationship with a dizzy blond song saleswoman. Features Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, with three numbers. This is where "Xango," "I Don't Care," and, "I Can't Get You Off My Mind." And this is where -- 1946 -- where Killian couldn't be shown.
Do you remember anything else about the "Idea Girl?"
Yeah. The girl that played the leading role in that -- her name was -- sang with us at the
Glenn Island Casino under the name of Laura Dean. And she was -- she played the leading role in that, the female lead.
What was her name then, I mean when she played the role?
I don't recall, but it wasn't Laura Dean.
They don't give the cast here.
She wouldn't even speak to me. She had her nose in the air the whole time. Which I thought was very funny, because --
She didn't want to be known as an ex-band singer?

I don't know. In our relationship there wasn't, you know, any trouble or anything. But she -- where she had been a very friendly girl, she was decidedly unfriendly. Could be that she didn't want anybody to know that she'd been a band singer, although I don't know what that would have to do with it.
